newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-SWISS COACH FORCED TO JUGGLE SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWISS COACH FORCED TO JUGGLE SQUAD.

text.p: Since announcing his squad to meet Norway in a World Cup qualifier on Saturday, Swiss coach Rolf Fringer has spent much of the week juggling his lineup because of injuries.
On Tuesday, he was forced to call up Grasshopper defender Pascal Thueler to replace Yvan Quentin who had injured his toe.
Also called up was Thueler's Grasshopper team mate and goalkeeper Pascal Zuberbueler who will take over the backup role from Joel Corminbeouf after he hurt his thigh.
With eight Grasshoppers now on the squad, Fringer is obviously hoping some of the success the Zurich side is enjoying in the Champions' League will rub off on his team against the Norwegians.
A sellout crowd of 22,000 supporters, anxious to get their first look at the Swiss squad, will be packed into Berne's Wankdorf Stadium.
The Swiss come into the match after beating Finland 3-2 although they lost 1-0 to Azerbaijan in their opening qualifier.
Norway top the group three table with six points followed by Switzerland, Hungary and Azerbaijan on three.
The Norwegians, with wins over Azerbaijan and Hungary, bring an attack to Switzerland that has produced eight goals in two matches and a defence that has allowed none.

Coach Egil Olsen has decided to use a 4-5-1 formation against the Swiss and accordingly Frank Strandli, Ole Gunnar Solskjear, Egil Oestenstad, Haavard Flo and Tore Andre Flo are all competing for the front-line striker position.
